summary: Builds the ACL FWS-RC corpus of future-work sentences from the full text of 4,024 NLP conference papers, with 3,067 manually annotated sentences. The sentences are coded into six main categories and 17 sub-categories, and their distribution is analysed. Automatic extraction and classification are stated as future work.
short_summary: Builds and classifies a corpus of future-work sentences from full-text NLP papers into six categories, with sub-categories.
rq_relation: RQ1: annotated future-work sentence corpus and taxonomy for sentence-level detection

summary: Proposes a regular-expression method to extract future-work sentences from computer science papers and defines four future-work categories. A multi-class classifier is compared with baselines, and a search prototype is built over the mined sentences. The abstract reports high precision and recall without giving numbers.
short_summary: Extracts future-work sentences with a regex method, classifies them into four categories, and builds a search prototype.
rq_relation: RQ1: regex baseline and four-category taxonomy for future-work sentence extraction

summary: Reviews LLM API pricing and outlines three cost-reduction strategies: prompt adaptation, LLM approximation and LLM cascade. Proposes FrugalGPT, a cascade that learns which LLM to query for each input. Reports matching GPT-4 performance at up to 98 percent lower cost, or 4 percent higher accuracy at equal cost.
short_summary: Proposes FrugalGPT, an LLM cascade that learns which models to query, cutting cost while matching or improving accuracy.
rq_relation: RQ2: cost and accuracy baseline for LLM cascades versus single-LLM prompting

summary: Introduces RULER, a synthetic long-context benchmark that extends needle-in-a-haystack with multiple needles, multi-hop tracing and aggregation tasks. Evaluating 17 long-context LMs on 13 tasks, most models drop sharply as length grows, and only half keep satisfactory performance at 32K. The benchmark is released as open source.
short_summary: Introduces RULER, a synthetic long-context benchmark showing that many LLMs degrade well before their claimed context sizes.
rq_relation: RQ3: evidence that LLMs degrade on long inputs beyond simple retrieval tests

summary: Runs a head-to-head human study with over 100 NLP researchers, comparing expert-written research ideas with an LLM ideation agent under blinded review. LLM ideas were judged more novel but slightly less feasible. The authors also report open problems, including weak LLM self-evaluation and low generation diversity.
short_summary: Human study finding LLM-generated research ideas judged more novel but less feasible than expert NLP researcher ideas.
rq_relation: Background for idea generation from mined gaps; little direct bearing on RQ1 to RQ3

summary: Compares a rule-based method using document structure, supervised classifiers (logistic regression and SVM) and self-training for recognising self-acknowledged limitation sentences in clinical articles. The rule-based method gives the best accuracy at 91.5 percent. Self-training gives only a small gain over supervised learning.
short_summary: Compares rule-based, supervised and self-training classifiers for recognising self-acknowledged limitation sentences in clinical literature.
rq_relation: RQ1: rule and classifier baselines for sentence-level limitation detection

summary: Benchmarks zero-shot text classification with unified datasets across topic, emotion and situation aspects, and adds a label-fully-unseen evaluation. Reformulates the task as textual entailment and provides state-of-the-art baselines. Code and data are released on GitHub.
short_summary: Benchmarks zero-shot text classification across aspects and reformulates it as textual entailment, with unified datasets and baselines.
rq_relation: RQ2: zero-shot NLI classification as a cheap filter stage in cascaded pipelines

summary: Creates a 15-category, 24-subcategory data model for self-acknowledged limitations in RCT publications and annotates 200 full-text articles. Fine-tunes PubMedBERT with EDA and PromDA augmentation for limitation sentence and type classification. The best model is applied to about 12K RCT publications, with type classification F1 near 0.7.
short_summary: Annotates RCT limitations with a data model, fine-tunes PubMedBERT with augmentation, and applies it to about 12K articles.
rq_relation: RQ1: fine-tuned BERT baseline and annotated corpus for sentence-level limitation detection

summary: Describes a dataset of 3,326 arXiv papers with LLM-extracted limitations, research gaps and importance statements, produced with LLaMA-3.3 and Mistral-Small through structured prompting. The abstract reports no validation of the extracted labels. It is presented as the first large-scale dataset for automated gap discovery.
short_summary: Dataset of 3,326 arXiv papers with LLM-extracted limitations, research gaps and importance statements.
rq_relation: RQ1: candidate resource for LLM-based gap extraction; label quality unvalidated

summary: Uses LDA topic modelling with cluster analysis, regression and network analysis on the ecological surrogates and indicators literature to track topic trends and research gaps. The authors argue that automated text analysis complements systematic reviews but must be used with care. The method is tested on a single conservation corpus.
short_summary: Uses LDA topic modelling and network analysis on indicator literature to identify research gaps in conservation science.
rq_relation: RQ1 background: corpus-level gap mapping via topic models, not sentence-level extraction

summary: Applies LDA topic modelling to 462 peer-reviewed articles on mining impacts in the Amazon from 1995 to 2025. Twelve topics are grouped into five categories, and co-occurrence and semantic similarity analyses reveal weakly connected topic pairs, such as monitoring indicators versus toxicology or biodiversity. It is a bibliometric synthesis of the field's research agenda.
short_summary: Applies LDA topic modelling to 462 Amazon mining articles to map themes and gaps in the literature.
rq_relation: RQ1 background: literature-level gap mapping via topic models, not sentence-level extraction

summary: Presents GapFinder, an open-source RAG pipeline that splits PDF text, retrieves segments and asks Qwen 2.5-7B or Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite to classify candidate research gaps. Each gap is labelled theoretical, methodological, empirical or contextual, with verbatim evidence and a suggestion. The abstract reports no evaluation.
short_summary: Open-source RAG tool using an LLM to classify candidate research gaps in articles with verbatim evidence and suggestions.
rq_relation: RQ1: LLM gap-extraction tool with evidence grounding; evaluation not reported in abstract

summary: Uses text mining of environmental science publications in Iran to identify research gaps and priorities. No abstract is available in the batch, so this summary rests on the title only. It is a bibliometric gap-mapping study rather than a sentence-level method.
short_summary: Uses text mining of environmental science publications in Iran to identify research gaps and priorities.
rq_relation: RQ1 background: literature-level gap mapping, limited relevance to sentence-level methods

summary: Proposes a system combining SciBERT and BioBERT embeddings, graph neural networks over citation structure, and SVM, random forest and gradient boosting classifiers to detect knowledge gaps. It targets discrepancies, voids and methodological limitations. The abstract claims 78 percent prediction accuracy and 88 percent expert validation but gives no evaluation details.
short_summary: Proposes an NLP, GNN and ensemble-classifier system to detect knowledge gaps in literature; claimed results are unverified in abstract.
rq_relation: RQ1: broad gap-detection system; claimed metrics lack methodological detail

summary: Presents an LLM-based decision support system that extracts key points, limitations and aims from several papers, compares them in a structured format and ranks possible research gaps. The abstract describes design goals only, with no evaluation. It is a seminar presentation.
short_summary: Presents an LLM-based decision support system that extracts structured key points, limitations and ranked research gaps across papers.
rq_relation: RQ1: multi-paper LLM gap ranking; design described without evaluation

summary: Describes GapFinder, an NLP tool that extracts text from PDF scientific documents to identify potential research gaps. The paper covers the development, the processing methodology and a simulated corpus demonstration. It is framed for researchers and English language teaching.
short_summary: Describes GapFinder, an NLP tool that mines PDF articles to identify potential research gaps, with a simulated demonstration.
rq_relation: RQ1: NLP gap-mining tool; methods described without quantitative evaluation

summary: Describes a hybrid system with rule-based patterns, classical ML classifiers and graph analysis that detects methodological, empirical and theoretical limitations, later extended to eleven categories. Reports agreement with 19 domain experts on 600 papers (79 and 85 percent) and a 60 percent reduction in review time in a beta study with 45 researchers. These results are self-reported in the abstract.
short_summary: Describes a hybrid rule, ML and graph system detecting eleven gap categories, validated against 19 experts on 600 papers.
rq_relation: RQ1: rule plus ML limitation detector with expert agreement; comparison baseline

summary: Introduces ATR4CH, a five-step methodology for LLM-based extraction from cultural heritage texts into knowledge graphs. Evaluated on Wikipedia articles about disputed items with Claude Sonnet 3.7, Llama 3.3 70B and GPT-4o-mini, reaching F1 of 0.65 to 0.99 depending on the task. Smaller models perform competitively, but human oversight is still needed.
short_summary: Five-step methodology for LLM-based knowledge graph extraction from cultural heritage texts, evaluated on Wikipedia authenticity debates with three LLMs.
rq_relation: RQ3 background: smaller LLMs competitive for scholarly-debate extraction; hypothesis extraction tangential

summary: Evaluates commercial and open-weight LLMs for technical term identification on ACL RD-TEC 2.0 against double human annotations. The best LLM reaches 76.6 percent F1, close to the 81.6 percent inter-human agreement. LLMs reliably extract terms humans agree on but omit disputed ones, and 30B-scale open models do well.
short_summary: Compares LLM term identification with double human annotations on ACL RD-TEC 2.0, finding LLMs omit terms that humans disagree on.
rq_relation: RQ1 background: LLM conservatism on borderline cases, relevant to gold-standard design

summary: Reports a pipeline using RAG, few-shot JSON-schema extraction and RDF mapping with gpt-4o-mini to extract scholarly interpretations from five articles on a medieval authorship debate. Outputs were checked against competency questions and expert review. The authors note that hedged claims are flattened into definite triples.
short_summary: RAG and gpt-4o-mini pipeline extracts scholarly interpretations from five articles into nanopublications, noting loss of hedged claims.
rq_relation: RQ1 background: LLM extraction loses hedging qualifiers, relevant to limitation phrasing

summary: Presents DocLap, a system combining layout parsing, multi-modal LLM correction, ontology constraint checks and RAG over graph and vector representations of multi-page scholarly documents. It supports semantic retrieval and question answering. Evaluation covers segmentation, error detection and retrieval, with details not given in the abstract.
short_summary: Integrated system for layout parsing and LLM-based question answering over multi-page scholarly documents, using RAG to handle long inputs.
rq_relation: RQ3: RAG as a workaround for LLM context-length limits on scholarly documents

summary: Presents MOLE, a schema-driven LLM framework that extracts metadata from entire scientific papers across input formats, with validation mechanisms. It introduces a benchmark and analyses context length, few-shot learning and web browsing. Modern LLMs show promising but inconsistent results, and the authors call for further work. Code and dataset are released.
short_summary: Schema-driven LLM framework extracts metadata from full scientific papers, analyzing context length and few-shot effects, with a new benchmark.
rq_relation: RQ3: document-level LLM extraction with explicit context-length analysis on scientific papers

summary: Uses LLMs to thematically synthesise 109 articles on social media deepfakes and maps the themes onto news articles from GDELT with topic modelling. Identifies a structural reactivity gap, where research overemphasises forensic detection and neglects digital literacy. The domain differs from the methods questions of this review.
short_summary: Uses LLMs to thematically analyze 109 deepfake articles and identifies a structural reactivity gap in the literature.
rq_relation: RQ1 background: LLM-assisted literature gap synthesis; domain differs

summary: Proposes a small academic-domain language model, continually pretrained on survey papers and attention-steered, to fact-check a general LLM's extraction of objectives and methods. Experiments on fake news detection and bibliometrics show it outperforms general LLMs on accuracy, stability and importance. Knowledge graph construction is listed as future work.
short_summary: Continually pretrained small language model acts as fact-checker for general LLM outputs when extracting objectives and methods from academic papers.
rq_relation: RQ2: small model verifying LLM outputs, a reverse-direction small-plus-LLM pipeline

summary: Uses generative AI and LLMs to extract entity-relation triples from 1,367 Taiwan-based China studies articles and builds a D3.js knowledge graph and vector database. The graph is intended to reveal thematic clusters and research gaps. The abstract gives no quantitative evaluation of extraction accuracy.
short_summary: Extracts entity-relation triples from Taiwan China studies articles with LLMs and visualizes a knowledge graph to surface research gaps.
rq_relation: RQ1 background: corpus-level gap discovery via LLM triple graphs

summary: Presents Repuatix, a six-agent LangGraph pipeline that retrieves citation records, extracts citation contexts, filters by MiniLM embedding relevance and classifies sentiment, intent and certainty with LLaMA3. Favourable and neutral citations are distinguished well, while critical citations are harder. The evaluation is qualitative in the abstract.
short_summary: Multi-agent LangGraph framework classifies citation sentiment and intent, using embedding relevance filtering before LLaMA3 classification.
rq_relation: RQ2: embedding relevance filter then LLM classification, an example of a small-filter cascade

summary: Combines ETL pipelines and hybrid RAG with agentic self-correction to extract fields from literature into Neo4j and Qdrant stores. Structured field extraction beats PDF chunking on semantic similarity, and the system is applied to ozone and cardiovascular literature to identify methodological gaps. Citation accuracy is 99 percent in validated responses.
short_summary: Combines ETL and hybrid RAG with agentic self-correction to extract fields and identify methodological research gaps from scholarly literature.
rq_relation: RQ3: structured extraction versus chunking for retrieval; RQ1: methodological gap identification

summary: Classifies the sentiment of citation statements referencing nine software engineering papers, using unsupervised machine learning. Uses generative AI to summarise the strengths and limitations of each target paper from clustered citation groups and full text. Compares external citation feedback with the authors' own presentation.
short_summary: Classifies citation sentiment and uses generative AI to summarize strengths and limitations of nine software engineering papers.
rq_relation: RQ1 background: limitations inferred from citation contexts rather than author-stated text

summary: Builds a pipeline in which a logistic regression classifier filters clinical notes and a 4-bit Llama-3.1-8B extracts mean sleep latency at several temperatures. Dynamic programming chooses the cascade of runs that maximises accuracy under a cost budget. Filtering cuts hallucinations and misses, and the optimised cascade lowers the miss rate further.
short_summary: Classifier filters clinical notes, then dynamic programming selects LLM temperature runs under a cost budget to extract mean sleep latency with fewer hallucinations.
rq_relation: RQ2: classifier filter plus budgeted LLM cascade shows the accuracy-cost tradeoff on clinical extraction

summary: Shows that LLMs underperform fine-tuned small models on nine IE datasets across four tasks, with higher latency and cost. Proposes an adaptive filter-then-rerank paradigm in which small models filter and an LLM reranks hard samples, giving about 2.4 F1 gain on average at acceptable cost. Code is released.
short_summary: Shows LLMs underperform fine-tuned small models on information extraction, then proposes an SLM-filter, LLM-rerank paradigm that improves F1 at acceptable cost.
rq_relation: RQ2: direct evidence for small-model filter then LLM; RQ3: weak LLM few-shot extraction
